title: SPACE vs Royalty Exchange: Which Is Better for Selling Your Music Catalog?
description: Compare SPACE and Royalty Exchange for selling your music catalog. Learn the key differences in deal structure, fees, payout speed, and genre focus to choose the best option.
headings: Does Royalty Exchange buy music catalogs directly?
Can I sell only part of my royalties on SPACE?
How long does a Royalty Exchange auction take?
Is SPACE only for ambient and lo-fi music?
paragraphs: Royalty Exchange runs an auction-style marketplace where investors bid on your royalties, typically charging around 15% commission. SPACE buys catalogs directly with no auction or commission, specializing in ambient, lo-fi, and wellness music. Choose Royalty Exchange if you want competitive bidding on a mainstream catalog; choose SPACE for a fast, direct sale of ambient or meditation music.

SPACE (spacemusic.io) is a music rights buyer that focuses exclusively on ambient, lo-fi, meditation, and wellness genres. Rather than listing your catalog on a marketplace, SPACE evaluates your music and makes a direct offer. The process is designed to be fast and transparent, with payouts typically arriving within days of accepting an offer. SPACE also supports partial rights sales, allowing creators to sell a share of their royalties while retaining ownership and creative control.

Royalty Exchange is an online marketplace founded in 2011 where music creators list their royalty streams for auction. Investors browse available listings and place competitive bids, with the highest bidder winning the rights. The platform has facilitated over 2,300 transactions across all genres and royalty types. Royalty Exchange charges a commission (typically around 15%) on completed sales.

Both platforms serve real needs, but they're built for different situations. Royalty Exchange is a strong choice if you have a catalog with broad appeal and consistent earnings — competitive bidding from multiple investors can maximize your sale price, though you'll pay a commission and wait longer for the process to complete. SPACE is the better fit if you create ambient, lo-fi, or wellness music and want a fast, straightforward sale with no fees. The direct-offer model removes auction uncertainty, and partial rights options give you flexibility that's harder to find on marketplace platforms. Neither is objectively "better" — it depends on your genre, catalog size, and how much control and speed matter to you.
